name: FORECAST.LINEAR
description: FORECAST.LINEAR predicts a future y-value along a linear trend line fitted by least squares to known x- and y-values. It is the recommended replacement for the legacy FORECAST function.
tldr: Predicts a y-value from a linear regression at a given x (Excel 2016+).

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The x-value at which to predict the corresponding y-value.

parameters.name: known_ys
parameters.description: The dependent (y) values of the known data used to fit the line.

parameters.name: known_xs
parameters.description: The independent (x) values of the known data; must match the size of known_ys.

basicExample.description: Predict the next value on a rising trend
basicExample.explanation: The fitted line is y = -1 + 2.2x, so at x=6 the prediction is -1 + 2.2*6 = 12.2.

advancedExamples.title: Forecast from worksheet ranges
advancedExamples.description: Use a column of past revenues and a column of period numbers
advancedExamples.explanation: Least-squares line through the 11 points is extended to x=13.

advancedExamples.title: Equivalence to legacy FORECAST
advancedExamples.explanation: FORECAST.LINEAR replaced FORECAST but computes identically.

howItWorks: FORECAST.LINEAR fits a straight line y = a + bx by least squares, with slope b = Σ((x - x̄)(y - ȳ)) / Σ(x - x̄)² and intercept a = ȳ - b·x̄, then evaluates that line at x. It is the modern, clearly named form of the legacy FORECAST function.

howToSteps.name: List known data
howToSteps.text: Place known x-values and known y-values in equal-length ranges.

howToSteps.name: Pick target x
howToSteps.text: Decide the x at which you want a prediction.

limitations: Models only a linear relationship; curved trends need TREND/GROWTH or transforms.
known_xs and known_ys must have the same number of points, or #N/A is returned.
If the x-values have no variance (all equal), the function returns #DIV/0!.

commonErrors.cause: known_xs and known_ys have different sizes, or a non-numeric x was supplied.
commonErrors.fix: Make the two arrays the same length and pass a numeric x.

commonErrors.cause: All known_xs values are identical, so the slope is undefined.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports FORECAST.LINEAR with identical behavior (and also FORECAST).

faq.question: Is FORECAST.LINEAR the same as FORECAST?
faq.answer: Yes. FORECAST.LINEAR is the modern name for the same calculation as the legacy FORECAST.

faq.question: Which should I use in new work?
faq.answer: Use FORECAST.LINEAR; FORECAST is retained only for backward compatibility.

faq.question: How is this different from TREND?
faq.answer: FORECAST.LINEAR returns a single predicted y; TREND can return an entire array of predictions at once.
